prompt: A teammate has opened a PR adding a second-pass summariser to the review engine. The proposed file is in FIXTURE_DIR — treat it as `reviewer-core/src/review/summarize.ts` in this repository. Review this PR before it is merged. Report every problem you find, most important first; for each one give the file and line, say what is wrong, and say what should be done about it. Write your review as markdown to OUTPUT_DIR/review.md.
assertions: Identifies that the file constructs its own LLM provider / reads an API key instead of taking an injected provider
Identifies that the file performs filesystem I/O, which this package must not do
Identifies that findings are returned without passing through the grounding gate
Does NOT flag the existing llm/openrouter.ts openai SDK import as a violation
Every reported problem cites a specific file and line

planted.text: summarize.ts reads process.env.OPENROUTER_API_KEY (line 39) and constructs its own OpenRouterProvider (line 41) instead of accepting an injected `llm: LLMProvider`
planted.rule: reviewer-core never constructs providers or reads keys; the LLMProvider arrives injected

planted.text: summarize.ts imports node:fs/promises (line 1) and reads skill bodies off disk (line 45) instead of receiving resolved strings from the caller
planted.rule: reviewer-core has zero filesystem/DB/GitHub access; inputs arrive as data

planted.text: summarize.ts returns result.data.findings straight from the model (line 64) without routing them through groundFindings()
planted.rule: the citation-grounding gate is a mandatory domain invariant for diff-anchored findings

decoys.text: reviewer-core/src/llm/openrouter.ts imports the `openai` SDK directly inside the pure package
decoys.why_not_a_bug: documented deliberate exception — it is a concrete adapter owned by the engine because both consumers need it, and it is only ever constructed at each consumer's composition root

legitimate_extra_findings: assemblePrompt is called with the wrong argument/return shape (it takes diff: string and returns {messages, assembly}, not {system, user})
completeStructured is called without the required schemaName / messages fields of StructuredRequest
z.custom<Finding>() disables runtime validation when Finding is a real Zod schema exported as a value
raw skill bodies are interpolated without formatSkillBlocks/wrapUntrusted prompt-injection wrapping
hardcoded model and timeout rather than caller-supplied
answer_key.grading_note: These are genuine defects in the fixture code, found during run 1. They are NOT false positives and must NOT count against precision. Only count a finding as a false positive if it targets a listed decoy or asserts a rule this repository does not hold.
